files.sha256: see git: the processor is JUCE glue; the parameter layout (:19-58), decay/size/damping law (:141-152), pre-delay (:157-174), freeze muting (:170, :187) and linear mix (:186-189) are reproduced line for line
deviations: juce::dsp::Reverb -> freeverb.h (Freeverb as juce::Reverb configures it, written JUCE-free)
juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Linear> -> EtherReverbDevice::PredelayLine (same push/pop semantics, 32768 samples)
mix and the freeze dry-mute ramp over 5 ms per sample (Ether steps them per block)
the reverb parameters are applied before the sample rate is set, so there is no 10 ms ramp from juce::Reverb's constructor defaults at start

JUCE_UNDENORMALISE (x += 0.1f; x -= 0.1f) -> livemix::flush_denormal: the 0.1f quantisation leaves the comb loop in a -116 dBFS limit cycle after every tail; flushing at 1e-15 lets it reach exact zero
juce::SmoothedValue<float> -> Freeverb::LinearRamp (same linear ramp semantics, 10 ms)

source.note: Ether's own DSP is juce::dsp::Reverb, i.e. Freeverb (Jezar, public domain) with JUCE's constants: comb tunings {1116,1188,1277,1356,1422,1491,1557,1617}, allpass {556,441,341,225}, stereo spread 23, integer rate scaling, input gain 0.015, feedback = roomSize*0.28+0.7, damping*0.4, allpass 0.5, wet 3 / dry 2, freeze = feedback 1 / damping 0 / input 0. freeverb.h is that algorithm; ether_reverb_device.* is Ether's processBlock; device_api.cpp is the ABI shim.
